def write(path, content, *, root=None):
    path = Path(path)
    require(not path.is_symlink(), "Refusing symlink output: " + str(path))
    if root is not None:
        resolved = private_location(path)
        require(Path(root).resolve() in resolved.parents, "Private output must remain inside its own folder: " + str(path))
        path = resolved
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    temp = path.with_name(path.name + "." + uuid.uuid4().hex + ".tmp")
    try:
        with temp.open("x", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            handle.write(content)
        os.replace(temp, path)
    finally:
        temp.unlink(missing_ok=True)

def source_targets(request):
    targets = request.get("source_targets", [])
    require(isinstance(targets, list), "source_targets must be a list")
    seen = set()
    for target in targets:
        require(isinstance(target, dict), "Each source target must be an object")
        require(target.get("kind") in ("workspace", "jira", "bitbucket_pr", "document", "web"), "Unknown source kind")
        ref = text(target.get("ref"), "Source reference")
        key = (target["kind"], ref)
        require(key not in seen, "Duplicate source target")
        seen.add(key)
    return targets

source_units.code:
def roster(request):
    require(isinstance(request, dict), "Request must be an object")
    source_targets(request)
    skill_lessons(request)
    for key in FIELDS:
        text(request.get(key), key)
    kind = request.get("analysis_type")
    require(kind in LENSES, "analysis_type must be architecture, planning or rca")
    text(request.get("framing_reply"), "The user's framing/model choice")
    selection = request.get("model_selection")
    require(isinstance(selection, dict) and selection.get("confirmed") is True, "Model roster needs the user's choice")
    require(selection.get("profile") in ("economy", "balanced", "thorough", "custom"), "Unknown model profile")
    text(selection.get("checked_at"), "Availability check date")
    text(selection.get("availability_source"), "Availability source")
    available = selection.get("catalog")
    require(isinstance(available, list) and bool(available), "Current model catalog is missing")
    catalog = {}
    for entry in available:
        require(isinstance(entry, dict), "Catalog entry must be an object")
        name = text(entry.get("model"), "Catalog model")
        require(name not in catalog, "Duplicate model in catalog")
        efforts = entry.get("efforts", [])
        require(isinstance(efforts, list) and all(isinstance(e, str) and e.strip() for e in efforts), "Invalid supported efforts")
        catalog[name] = efforts
    assignments = selection.get("roles", {})
    require(isinstance(assignments, dict), "roles must be an object")

    def assignment(value):
        require(isinstance(value, dict), "Each role needs a model assignment")
        name = text(value.get("model"), "Assigned model")
        require(name in catalog and name.lower().strip() not in ("auto", "inherit"), "Select an explicit available model: " + name)
        result = {"model": name}
        if "effort" in value:
            require(value["effort"] in catalog[name], "Unsupported effort for " + name)
            result["effort"] = value["effort"]
        return result

    groups = {role: assignment(assignments.get(role)) for role in ("grounding", "workers", "outflanker", "chair")}
    overrides = selection.get("worker_overrides", {})
    require(isinstance(overrides, dict) and set(overrides) <= set(LENSES[kind]), "Unknown worker override")
    result = {"grounding": groups["grounding"]}
    for lens in LENSES[kind]:
        result[lens] = assignment(overrides[lens]) if lens in overrides else dict(groups["workers"])
    result.update({"outflanker": groups["outflanker"], "chair": groups["chair"]})
    binding = request.get("binding", {})
    require(isinstance(binding, dict) and binding.get("mode") in ("tool-model", "custom-agent"), "Bind models through tool-model or custom-agent")
    text(binding.get("host"), "Execution host")
    text(binding.get("verified_by"), "How the model binding capability was checked")
    tools = binding.get("grounding_tools")
    require(isinstance(tools, list) and bool(tools) and all(isinstance(t, str) and t.strip() for t in tools), "List the host's available read/research tools for grounding")
    if any("effort" in model for model in result.values()):
        require(binding["mode"] == "tool-model", "Per-role effort requires tool-model binding; custom-agent uses provider defaults")
        require(binding.get("supports_effort") is True, "Per-role effort requires binding.supports_effort=true after checking the host control; otherwise omit role effort and use provider defaults")
    return result

def initialize(root, request):
    selected = roster(request)
    root = private_directory(root)
    runs = private_location(root / "runs")
    require(runs == root / "runs", "The runs folder must not redirect private cases to another location")
    run_id = datetime.now(timezone.utc).strftime("%Y%m%d-%H%M%S-") + uuid.uuid4().hex[:10]
    run = runs / run_id
    run.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=False)
    state = {"version": 1, "run_id": run_id, "created_at": now(), "personal_root": str(root), "request": request, "roster": selected,
             "results": {}, "attempts": {}, "failures": {}, "receipts": [], "factbase_digest": None,
             "fact_review": None, "bindings": {}, "retry_notes": {}}
    save(run, state)
    return {"run": str(run), **next_step(run, state, ["grounding"])}

def load(run):
    run = private_location(run)
    state = read_json(run / "state.json")
    require(state.get("version") == 1, "Unsupported run version")
    root = private_location(state.get("personal_root", run.parent.parent))
    require(run == root / "runs" / state["run_id"], "Run moved outside its configured personal folder; inspect the location before continuing")
    require(roster(state["request"]) == state["roster"], "Run roster does not match its request")
    require(digest(run / "report.md") == state["report_digest"], "Saved report changed or a write was interrupted; inspect the run before continuing")
    for receipt in state["receipts"]:
        require(digest(run / receipt["file"]) == receipt["sha256"], "A submitted response was modified; use a new run for changed evidence")
    if state["factbase_digest"]:
        require(digest(run / "factbase.json") == state["factbase_digest"], "Factbase changed after submission; create a new run for revised evidence")
        require(digest(run / "factbase.md") == state["factbase_markdown_digest"], "Displayed factbase changed after submission")
    return state

def validate_coverage(output, state):
    coverage = output.get("source_coverage", [])
    require(isinstance(coverage, list), "source_coverage must be a list")
    expected = {(t["kind"], t["ref"]) for t in source_targets(state["request"])}
    received = set()
    for item in coverage:
        require(isinstance(item, dict), "Each coverage entry must be an object")
        for key in ("kind", "ref", "as_of", "detail"):
            text(item.get(key), "Source coverage " + key)
        key = (item["kind"], item["ref"])
        require(key in expected and key not in received, "Unknown or duplicate source coverage")
        require(item.get("status") in ("read", "partial", "unavailable"), "Invalid source access status")
        received.add(key)
    require(received == expected, "Account for every requested source, including inaccessible sources")
    return coverage

source_units.code:
def submit(run, role, response):
    run = Path(run)
    with locked(run):
        state = load(run)
        # Other workers from an already-dispatched batch may finish after a sibling fails.
        previous_status = phase(state)[0]
        ready = phase({**state, "failures": {}})[1]
        require(role in ready and role not in state["failures"], "Role is not ready for a result: " + role)
        require(state["attempts"].get(role, 0) < attempt_limit(state, role), "Retry limit reached")
        attempt = state["attempts"].get(role, 0) + 1
        state["attempts"][role] = attempt
        receipt_path = "responses/" + role + "-" + str(attempt) + ".json"
        write(run / receipt_path, encode(response), root=run)
        record = {"role": role, "attempt": attempt, "file": receipt_path, "sha256": digest(run / receipt_path), "requested": dict(state["roster"][role]), "accepted": False, "execution": {}}
        if role == "grounding":
            state.pop("source_attempt_coverage", None)
        error = None
        try:
            require(isinstance(response, dict), "Response envelope must be an object")
            execution = response.get("execution")
            require(isinstance(execution, dict), "Missing host execution record")
            call_id = text(execution.get("call_id"), "Host/tool call ID")
            require(all(r["execution"].get("call_id") != call_id for r in state["receipts"]), "An agent call ID cannot stand for two roles or attempts")
            record["execution"] = execution
            require(execution.get("requested_model") == state["roster"][role]["model"], "Invocation model differs from the selected model")
            require(execution.get("binding_mode") == state["request"]["binding"]["mode"], "Invocation binding mode differs")
            # attempt has already been incremented; the launched name used the previous count.
            expected_name = "council-" + state["run_id"] + "-" + role.replace("_", "-") + "-" + str(attempt)
            if execution["binding_mode"] == "custom-agent":
                require(execution.get("agent_name") == expected_name, "Wrong custom agent invoked")
                binding = state["bindings"].get(expected_name)
                require(binding and Path(binding["path"]).is_file() and digest(binding["path"]) == binding["sha256"], "Custom-agent definition is missing or changed")
            if "effort" in state["roster"][role]:
                require(execution.get("requested_effort") == state["roster"][role]["effort"], "Invocation effort differs")
            if execution.get("observed_model") is not None:
                text(execution["observed_model"], "Observed model")
                text(execution.get("model_evidence"), "Host model evidence")
                require(execution["observed_model"] == state["roster"][role]["model"], "Observed model differs; check the mapping with the user instead of accepting a fallback")
            require(not response.get("error"), str(response.get("error")))
            if role == "grounding" and isinstance(response.get("output"), dict):
                # Preserve reported access gaps even when there are too few facts to proceed.
                state["source_attempt_coverage"] = validate_coverage(response["output"], state)
            output = validate_output(role, response.get("output"), state)
            state["results"][role] = output
            record["accepted"] = True
            if role == "grounding":
                write(run / "factbase.json", encode(output), root=run)
                state["factbase_digest"] = digest(run / "factbase.json")
                lines = ["# Factbase", "", output["brief"], ""]
                for fact in output["facts"]:
                    lines += [f"## {fact['id']}. {fact['fact']}", f"Source: {fact['source']}", f"Status: {fact['status']} · As-of: {fact['as_of']}", ""]
                lines += coverage_lines(output)
                write(run / "factbase.md", "\n".join(lines), root=run)
                state["factbase_markdown_digest"] = digest(run / "factbase.md")
        except Invalid as exc:
            error = str(exc)
            state["failures"][role] = error
            record["error"] = error
        state["receipts"].append(record)
        save(run, state)
        new_status, ready_roles = phase(state)
        # Deliver a newly available stage once; don't repeat sibling prompts after each return.
        new_jobs = ready_roles if new_status != previous_status and ready_roles else None
        return {"accepted": error is None, "error": error, **next_step(run, state, new_jobs)}

def retry(run, role, new_selection=None, reply=None):
    with locked(run):
        state = load(run)
        require(role in state["failures"] and state["attempts"].get(role, 0) < attempt_limit(state, role), "No retry available for this role")
        if new_selection is not None:
            text(reply, "User's replacement-model choice")
            candidate = {**state["request"], "model_selection": new_selection}
            revised = roster(candidate)
            require(all(revised[r] == state["roster"][r] for r in revised if r != role), "A retry may change only the failed role; completed assignments stay intact")
            state["request"] = candidate
            state["roster"] = revised
            state.setdefault("model_changes", []).append({"role": role, "reply": reply, "at": now()})
        state["retry_notes"][role] = state["failures"].pop(role)
        save(run, state)
        return next_step(run, state, [role] if not state['failures'] else None)

def revise(run, critique):
    text(critique, "User's revision request")
    with locked(run):
        state = load(run)
        require(phase(state)[0] == "complete" and not state.get("revision"), "One chair revision is available only after initial completion")
        write(Path(run) / "history/report-before-revision.md", (Path(run) / "report.md").read_text(encoding="utf-8"), root=run)
        write(Path(run) / "history/state-before-revision.json", encode(state), root=run)
        state["revision"] = {"critique": critique, "at": now(), "attempt": state["attempts"]["chair"] + 1,
                             "previous_chair": state["results"].pop("chair")}
        state["retry_notes"].pop("chair", None)
        save(run, state)
        return next_step(run, state, ["chair"])

def clean_agents(run):
    with locked(run):
        state = load(run)
        require(phase(state)[0] in ("complete", "failed"), "Do not remove bindings from an active run")
        for item in state["bindings"].values():
            path = Path(item["path"])
            require(not path.is_symlink(), "A generated binding became a symlink")
            require(not path.exists() or digest(path) == item["sha256"], "A generated binding was edited; preserve it")
        removed = []
        for item in state["bindings"].values():
            path = Path(item["path"])
            if path.exists():
                path.unlink()
                removed.append(str(path))
        state["bindings_cleaned_at"] = now()
        save(run, state)
        return {"removed": removed}

def learn(run, entry):
    """Append a confirmed method improvement; keep case results in run files."""
    require(isinstance(entry, dict) and entry.get("confirmed") is True, "A lesson needs the user's confirmation")
    require(entry.get("purpose") == "skill_improvement", "The KB is for Decision Council skill learning, not case results")
    require(set(entry) == {"purpose", "confirmed", "lesson", "context", "limits", "confirmation"}, "Only skill-learning fields are allowed; save results in the run report")
    for key in ("lesson", "context", "limits", "confirmation"):
        text(entry.get(key), "Lesson " + key)
    run = Path(run).resolve()
    with locked(run):
        state = load(run)
        require(phase(state)[0] in ("complete", "failed"), "Finish the review before recording its lesson")
        root = private_directory(state.get("personal_root", run.parent.parent))
        require(run.parent.parent == root, "Personal root differs from this run's location")
        identity = {key: " ".join(entry[key].split()).casefold() for key in ("lesson", "context", "limits")}
        lesson_id = hashlib.sha256(encode(identity).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:20]
        marker = "<!-- council-lesson:" + lesson_id + " -->"
        kb = root / "council_kb.md"
        # The root lock serializes KB writes across different run folders.
        with locked(root):
            require(not kb.is_symlink(), "Personal KB is a symlink; preserve it and choose a regular KB file")
            existing = kb.read_text(encoding="utf-8") if kb.exists() else KB_HEADER
            if marker in existing:
                return {"saved": False, "already_present": True, "knowledge_base": str(kb), "lesson_id": lesson_id}
            record = "\n\n" + marker + "\n## " + now() + " · " + lesson_id + "\n\n" + entry["lesson"].strip()
            record += "\n\nContext: " + entry["context"].strip() + "\n\nLimits: " + entry["limits"].strip()
            record += "\n\nPurpose: Decision Council skill improvement · User confirmed\n\nOriginating run: " + state["run_id"] + "\n"
            # The actual reply may mention case results; preserve it in the run, not the KB.
            write(run / "learning" / (lesson_id + ".json"), encode({**entry, "recorded_at": now(), "lesson_id": lesson_id}), root=run)
            write(kb, existing + record, root=root)
        return {"saved": True, "already_present": False, "knowledge_base": str(kb), "lesson_id": lesson_id}

---
name: decision-council
author: Roland Chotika
description: Stress-test an uncertain architecture, plan, or root-cause thesis with seven independent agent calls, a human fact review and a saved verdict. Use for an explicit council or substantive adversarial decision review; propose available models and let the user choose.
metadata:
  version: "0.6.1-portable-candidate"
license: MIT
---

# Decision Council

Keep the method: **grounding → human fact review → four blind workers → outflanker
→ chair**. Seven real native agent calls, possibly one model in separate contexts.
A simple lookup needs no Decision Council. Reviewing does not authorize changing the subject.
The main chat owns questions and integration; the Python 3.10+ standard-library
coordinator owns jobs, checks and private reports. It makes no model/API calls.

## Frame and choose

1. Reuse supplied context and clarify only material gaps, especially the review
   boundary. Select `architecture`, `planning` or `rca`. Establish question, goal,
   reason for Decision Council, primary sources, success criterion, thesis, meaningful
   antithesis, scope and non-goal; choose the user's response language.
2. Agree a personal folder outside Git and this skill on first use; `configure`
   remembers it and preserves the KB. Keep requests/results there. Read relevant
   [seed guidance](kb/council_kb.md) and personal method lessons, never case facts
   or old verdicts as evidence. For source access or learning, read only the needed
   section of [sources and learning](references/sources-and-knowledge.md).
3. Before model proposals, read [model selection](references/model-selection.md).
   Check actual availability and native binding. Show concrete Economy, Balanced
   and Thorough rosters, recommend one and allow role/lens overrides. Profiles
   retain seven roles. Auto in the main chat does not select explicit role models.

**Checkpoint 1:** show scope, thesis/antithesis and concrete models. Wait for the
user's framing/model choice; reuse an explicit choice already made for this run.
Never manufacture consent or silently replace a model.

## Execute from saved progress

Read [binding: host check and request](references/execution-binding.md#check-the-actual-host-first)
when preparing execution. Resolve the actual native tool and model controls; if they
cannot provide separate contexts and the selected models, explain the limitation
before calls. No simulated returns or prompt-only model selection.

Run `scripts/council_run.py` with the chosen interpreter. `init` starts the approved
request; `next --run <run>` resumes. Newly available stages return full jobs once; intermediate worker submissions and
`next` return compact metadata. Dispatch full jobs unchanged. After interruption,
retrieve missing prompts with `next --run <run> --role <role>`; repeat `--role`
for an independent batch. Never dispatch a metadata-only job.
The binding guide supplies request/envelope syntax; load failure/revision sections
only when needed. Do not reread the full guide on every step.

| Returned status | Main agent action |
| --- | --- |
| `grounding` | Start its native read-only job. It returns a neutral brief without recommendations, 3–14 sourced facts and coverage of every requested source. Evidence gaps belong in that basis; clarification blocks only when a substantive basis cannot be established, not merely when a verdict is uncertain. Submit the actual response; the runner writes the factbase. |
| `awaiting-fact-review` | **Show brief, facts, source coverage and uncertainty; ask for review and wait.** Flag any recommendation in the brief as outside grounding's role, never as a fact. Then `approve-facts` with the exact digest and actual reply. Revised evidence/frame requires a new run. |
| `workers` | Dispatch four separate, mutually blind lens contexts with the complete approved facts and sources. Parallel calls are allowed; submit serially. No research or overall verdict by workers. |
| `outflanker` | After all four valid returns, dispatch its job to challenge the strongest claim/shared frame and propose a falsification check. |
| `chair` | Dispatch the full evidence and prior results. Require mechanism, remaining gap, decision trigger and plain-language walkthrough; undecidable is valid. |
| `failed` | Preserve results and incomplete report. Read binding's failure section; at most one retry per failed role, with explicit choice before changing its model. |
| `complete` | Read the intact saved report, present the chair's brief then verdict and report link, including limits and off-scope findings. |

Use raw structured returns and actual tool metadata. Do not rewrite a failed answer
into a passing one. Analysis roles with `tools: []` need full facts inline; a file path
is insufficient. Keep workers blind to siblings and main-chat history. Accept all
already-dispatched returns even if one fails; never reduce the worker count.

Analysis jobs carry all numbered facts and source coverage, excluding the grounding brief
to avoid carrying a premature recommendation into independent analysis. A worker with no
supported finding returns `lens`, `found: false` and `reason`; it needs no invented claim
or confidence. The runner preserves raw responses and validates any supplied fact references.

`next` revalidates saved integrity. Never edit state/digests to bypass failure or reset
retry limits. A requested chair-only revision uses `revise` once and preserves upstream
work; no automatic retry of that revision. Use `clean-agents` after all calls end and
no continuation needs generated bindings; edited files stay protected.

## Deliver and learn

Only `complete` establishes workflow completion; missing/invalid roles leave a saved
incomplete report. Requested and observed model identities are separate. Checks do
not prove factual truth, reply authenticity or an unexposed backend model.

After delivery offer one optional reflection on Decision Council's method. Save only a
user-supplied or confirmed process improvement with `learn`, using the learning
reference. Case facts, findings, verdicts and domain knowledge stay in run files,
not either KB. Shared seed files remain read-only during use.

[START-HERE.html](START-HERE.html) and
[demo.html](demo.html) explain use. Local tests do not establish live target-environment behavior.

# Decision Council skill learning

Read before framing. This KB improves how Decision Council works. It contains no case results, verdicts or
project knowledge. This packaged guidance is read-only during normal runs. User-confirmed method
improvements belong in the user's separate `council_kb.md` under their Decision Council output folder.

## Framing traps

- For a design proposal with no code yet, decide whether the mechanism alone or its future call sites are under review.
- For a component inside a larger system, ask whether surrounding behavior is in scope.
- For root-cause analysis, bound how far back the causal search should go; an upstream truth may be unactionable.
- For plan review, distinguish the sequencing of work from the content of the plan.
- If thesis and antithesis say the same thing, sharpen the decision before starting a council.
- If a question says “look at everything,” ask which decision the user needs to make.

## Lessons

- Pass scope and non-goal to every downstream seat. The chair should route findings that answer a different question to an off-scope appendix.
- Let the outflanker question the frame freely. A wider finding belongs in the verdict when it changes the answer to the asked question.
- Show a plain-language brief before the fact table so the human can review the actual dispute.
- Make the verdict understandable with a concrete walkthrough of the normal and failing cases when the mechanism is dense.
- Ask a framing question before drafting the user's frame. Approval of a prewritten frame can conceal a mistaken scope.
- Keep the factbase to the facts that could change the decision; repeated background facts add cost without signal.
- Distinguish intended behavior in a ticket or PR description from inspected code and executed checks.
- Match workspace and PR revisions before using local code as PR evidence; show mismatches and access gaps.

After a run, optionally record method improvements provided or confirmed by the user in their KB.
Include their context and limits. Keep the review's outcomes in its report. Updating this
packaged guidance is separate skill maintenance, not an automatic side effect of using Decision Council.

source_units.code:
# Independent role execution

This guide is for the main agent running Decision Council. The user chooses the question, boundary and
models in chat; the main agent handles the commands and JSON files. The skill is distributed
independently of any team repository or process.

## Check the actual host first

Requirements: Python 3.10+; file/terminal access for the coordinator; native independent agent calls;
and a verified way to bind the chosen model to each role. No model SDK, API token, package install,
server or daemon is needed. On some Windows hosts the Python command is `py -3`; on others it is
`python` or `python3`. Check the available interpreter and quote paths for the actual shell.

Execution environments expose different delegation tools.
Inspect the current tool schema and custom-agent discovery; do not invent a tool name or argument.
Use one of these bindings:

| Binding | Use when | Actual model control |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tool-model` | The exposed native delegation tool supports a model argument for this call | Pass the job's exact model through that argument. |
| `custom-agent` | Native delegation can select a discovered custom agent with its own model field | Export personal `.agent.md` files, verify discovery, and invoke the exact returned agent name. |

For `custom-agent`, use a personal agent directory explicitly recognized by the current environment.
This route requires support for the exported `.agent.md` format; it is not a universal installation format. Do not put personal run/model settings in a shared repository. Agent names
include the run, role and attempt to avoid collisions. Analysis agents declare `tools: []` and
`agents: []`; grounding receives only the actual available read/research tools recorded in the
request. Verify the host honors these restrictions. In tool-model mode, apply equivalent controls
when available and ensure analysis agents use no research or further delegation.

Per-call effort is optional: set it only in `tool-model` mode when both tool and model explicitly
support it. Record the checked host capability as `binding.supports_effort: true`, list the
supported values in each relevant catalog entry's `efforts`, and choose one in the role's `effort`.
For example, if the host and model support `medium`, use `"supports_effort": true` in `binding`,
`"efforts": ["medium"]` in that model's catalog entry, and `"effort": "medium"` in its role assignment.
Without that verified capability, omit role `effort`; do not set the flag just to pass validation.
The custom-agent route uses provider-default effort. Do not represent a prompt about
"thinking harder" as a runtime effort setting. Availability in the main model picker does not
establish availability to subagents, particularly across cost tiers or account policies.

If this host cannot bind models or create independent contexts, stop before model work and explain
what is missing. Offer a supported native route or an explicit single-model roster, still with seven
separate agents. Never silently inherit the parent model or simulate agent returns.

Independent calls must receive all required context in their job, not inherited chat history or sibling results. The main conversation owns both human checkpoints. Check whether the environment honors tool/delegation restrictions, exact model selection and account limits. Do not silently fall back. A host-specific installation or UI command is not part of this package's contract.

## Personal location and request

On first use, agree the location with the user and run:

```text
python3 <skill>/scripts/council_run.py configure --root <personal-folder>
```

The folder must be outside Git repositories and the distributed skill. The location pointer is
`~/.config/council/location.json` on macOS/Linux or `%APPDATA%/council/location.json` on Windows.
The existing personal `council_kb.md` is preserved. There are no personal files in the skill itself.
`init --root ...` can use a specific personal root without changing the remembered preference.

Save the approved request under the personal root. This example uses **placeholder models and tool
names**, not a catalog to copy. Replace every placeholder with current, checked values. Fields and
outputs may use the user's preferred language. The `framing_reply` is the user's real response to
the displayed scope and concrete roster, not a generated consent statement.

```json
{
  "question": "The decision to evaluate",
  "goal": "What the user wants to achieve",
  "why_council": "The meaningful uncertainty",
  "primary_sources": "Concrete local paths, URLs or supplied evidence",
  "success_criterion": "What would settle this decision",
  "thesis": "The proposed answer",
  "antithesis": "A meaningfully competing answer",
  "scope": "The agreed level and boundary",
  "non_goal": "What this decision does not address",
  "analysis_type": "architecture",
  "language": "English",
  "framing_reply": "The actual user reply",
  "binding": {
    "mode": "custom-agent",
    "host": "Actual execution environment and version",
    "verified_by": "Observed native tool schema and custom-agent discovery",
    "grounding_tools": ["ACTUAL_READ_TOOL", "ACTUAL_RESEARCH_TOOL"]
  },
  "model_selection": {
    "profile": "balanced",
    "confirmed": true,
    "checked_at": "Actual check date/time",
    "availability_source": "Observed tool result or user-reported model picker",
    "catalog": [{"model": "EXACT_MODEL_A"}, {"model": "EXACT_MODEL_B"}],
    "roles": {
      "grounding": {"model": "EXACT_MODEL_A"},
      "workers": {"model": "EXACT_MODEL_A"},
      "outflanker": {"model": "EXACT_MODEL_B"},
      "chair": {"model": "EXACT_MODEL_B"}
    },
    "worker_overrides": {}
  }
}
```

See [model selection](model-selection.md) for per-lens overrides and optional supported effort.
Do not retain secrets or unnecessary source content in availability evidence.
For workspace, IssueTracker and CodeReview reviews, also include `source_targets` from
[sources and skill learning](sources-and-knowledge.md). Add relevant Decision Council method improvements from the personal KB as
`skill_lessons` with `purpose: skill_improvement`. Both are assembled by the main conversation, not by the user. Ensure grounding can
access the required read tools or an attributed private source packet before initializing the run.

## Initialize and invoke jobs

```text
python3 <skill>/scripts/council_run.py init --request <request.json>
python3 <skill>/scripts/council_run.py next --run <returned-run-path>
```

`init` returns an absolute `run` path and the full grounding job. Keep the path.
`approve-facts` returns the four full worker jobs; finishing the last worker returns
the outflanker, then its submission returns the chair. Intermediate worker submissions
return metadata only, so sibling prompts are not repeated. `next` is compact by default.
After interruption, fetch only missing full prompts for dispatch:

```text
python3 <skill>/scripts/council_run.py next --run <run> --role grounding
python3 <skill>/scripts/council_run.py next --run <run> --role <lens-1> --role <lens-2> --role <lens-3> --role <lens-4>
```

Only currently pending roles can be fetched; workers remain unavailable before fact review.
Each fetched job retains the complete approved facts and source coverage. Dispatch the fetched
batch once; intermediate submission summaries are not instructions to re-launch siblings.
Do not pass a metadata-only job to an agent. With `custom-agent`, export bindings before calls:

```text
python3 <skill>/scripts/council_run.py export-agents --run <run> --directory <personal-agent-directory>
```

Verify the host discovered those exact agents, model fields and tool restrictions. Some hosts may
need an agent-list refresh; exporting a file alone is not proof of discovery. Do not invoke a generic
agent while claiming it used an exported definition. Re-export after a retry or chair revision;
only pending roles are exported and a new attempt gets a distinct name.

Each job includes `role`, `attempt`, `model`, optional `effort`, `binding_mode`, `agent_name`, `tools`
and the complete `prompt`. Invoke the actual native tool in an independent context with the full
prompt and either the explicit model argument or exact custom-agent name. Do not pass sibling
worker results or the main conversation history. Parallel worker calls are allowed; coordinator
writes must be serial. Wait for the real result of each native call.

## Submit actual returns

Save an envelope containing the actual host/tool invocation metadata and the agent's raw JSON:

```json
{
  "execution": {
    "call_id": "Unique identifier from the actual native call",
    "binding_mode": "custom-agent",
    "requested_model": "EXACT_MODEL_A",
    "agent_name": "Exact name returned in the job",
    "observed_model": null
  },
  "output": {"is_clarification": false, "brief": "Actual agent brief", "facts": []}
}
```

The empty `facts` array above only illustrates the envelope; real grounding requires 3–14 facts.
Every job prompt specifies that role's output schema. Do not repair or substitute an agent's answer
in the main chat to pass validation. If it returns malformed JSON, preserve the raw text in `output`
and let validation fail. For a failed call, use `output: null` and `error` with the real error text.
Do not fabricate a call when no native invocation occurred.

Workers use two response forms. A positive finding needs the complete finding fields in its
job. A no-finding response needs only `lens`, `found: false` and a nonempty `reason`; optional
`sources` must cite existing fact IDs, and `claim` must be absent or empty. Do not add confidence
or a claim to a raw no-finding return. The coordinator records all four responses and passes
the absence of findings to synthesis without treating it as a missing worker.

In `tool-model` mode omit `agent_name`; include `requested_effort` only if the job specifies it.
`observed_model` is optional or null. Add it, with `model_evidence`, only when actual host metadata
identifies the executed model. An agent's self-description is not evidence. If the observed name
conflicts with the selected name, validation stops: resolve alias/version mapping or a changed
assignment with the user before a retry. Never hide a fallback as the original model.

```text
python3 <skill>/scripts/council_run.py submit --run <run> --role <job-role> --response <response.json>
```

Commands emit JSON. Exit code 2 means an error or failed run, not completion. A pending worker from
an already-dispatched batch may still be submitted after a sibling fails; the overall run remains
failed until the issue is resolved. No outflanker or chair is dispatched from that failed state.

At `awaiting-fact-review`, show the returned brief, facts, `source_coverage` and uncertainty. After the user's
real acceptance of those exact facts:

```text
python3 <skill>/scripts/council_run.py approve-facts --run <run> --digest <returned-digest> --reply <actual-reply>
```

The four full jobs are returned once. Dispatch that batch and submit each actual result
serially; the last valid return supplies the next stage. Use `next --role` only to retrieve
a missing pending prompt after interruption. A retry returns only the retried job once
all failures are resolved; recover any other missing pending jobs with `next --role`.
Quote user text safely for the shell; never interpolate unescaped text into executable commands.

## Failures, retries and a requested revision

`next` is read-only and reconstructs pending work from persisted state. Do not rerun completed
roles. A `.lock` means another write may be active; inspect the process before removing a stale
lock. Do not edit `state.json`, receipts, factbase or report to bypass validation. Keep annotations
in a separate file. Interrupted writes or changed digests need inspection before continuation.

A failed role has one retry with its selected model:

```text
python3 <skill>/scripts/council_run.py retry --run <run> --role <failed-role>
```

If a model became unavailable, propose a replacement and get the user's choice. Save the full
revised `model_selection` record, changing only that failed role (use `worker_overrides` for one
worker), then:

```text
python3 <skill>/scripts/council_run.py retry --run <run> --role <failed-role> --selection <selection.json> --reply <actual-choice>
```

It consumes the same single retry allowance; completed roles and their evidence stay intact.
Do not initialize a fresh run solely to reset retry limits. New evidence or a changed question
warrants a new run with a fresh framing and fact review.

After a completed verdict, the user may request one chair-only revision:

```text
python3 <skill>/scripts/council_run.py revise --run <run> --critique <actual-user-critique>
```

This archives the earlier report/state under `history/`, retains all upstream results, and returns
one full chair job. A failed revision has no further retry. Model changes are not part
of this command.
Re-export the pending custom agent if applicable. An additional review with new evidence is a new run.

## Deliver, then remove temporary bindings

Only `complete` means all seven roles and the current chair verdict passed validation. Read the
saved report; deliver its plain-language brief first, then the verdict and report link. The report
contains all worker results, original sources, uncertainty and requested/observed models. Failed
runs remain available as explicitly incomplete reports. An earlier successful report remains linked
when a later requested revision fails.

When all calls have ended and their definitions are no longer needed:

```text
python3 <skill>/scripts/council_run.py clean-agents --run <run>
```

Only unchanged generated definitions are removed. Edited definitions are preserved. Reports,
responses, facts, model choices and personal lessons remain under the user's personal root.

Save a user-supplied or confirmed improvement to Decision Council's method with `learn --run <run> --entry <lesson.json>` using the
[learning contract](sources-and-knowledge.md#save-a-confirmed-lesson). This is a separate optional
step after delivery. The KB never stores case facts, findings, verdicts or project knowledge.
The actual confirmation stays in the run's learning receipt. Read relevant method improvements
before the next run and pass their context and limits through `skill_lessons`, separately from evidence.

## Verification boundary

Run the portable behavior suite without model-account credentials:

```text
python3 -m unittest discover -s <skill>/tests -p 'test_*.py' -v
```

These tests use synthetic agent responses and verify state, model contracts, sources and saved
artifacts. They do not establish live compatibility for every host/version or organization.
Before broad distribution, run one real Decision Council on the intended host: confirm discovery/model
binding, both human checkpoints, four isolated worker calls, full-source handoff, persisted report
and a clear failure for an unavailable model. These export candidates have not completed that live check.

source_units.code:
# Model selection

Read before the framing checkpoint. Choose models for this run, not a permanent
shared roster. Use the actual host/account catalog and delegation controls; a model
in the main picker is not necessarily available to subagents. Record exact names,
check date and availability source. If the agent cannot inspect the catalog, ask
once for the names shown in the user's picker and label them user-reported.
Do not change accounts/settings or infer entitlement from a public catalog.

## Propose and wait

Show three concrete rosters and recommend one with a short reason based on this
question's uncertainty, source complexity, consequences and usage constraints:

| Profile | Allocation |
| --- | --- |
| Economy | Efficient models for bounded work, retaining capable challenge and synthesis |
| Balanced | Reliable grounding/workers; more reasoning for outflanker/chair where useful |
| Thorough | Stronger grounding and analysis where the evidence or consequences justify it |

Name the grounding model, four workers (group identical choices), outflanker and
chair for each. Explain the expected usage/latency trade-off; do not invent prices
or claim seven agents means seven billed requests. If the catalog is small, profiles
may coincide. One model in seven separate contexts is valid; vendor diversity is
optional and is not proof of independence or quality.

Combine model choice with the scope/thesis checkpoint. Wait for the real reply.
“Balanced” accepts the concrete roster just shown. Reuse an explicit choice already
made for this run. Allow any role/lens override; explain concerns without silently
replacing the user's selection. All profiles retain every role and evidence gate.

## Bind and record

Use the actual model argument or a discovered custom agent's model field; see
[binding](execution-binding.md#check-the-actual-host-first). A model name in prompt
text is not binding. The main chat may use Auto, but Decision Council requires explicit role
models. If the user requests Auto for the roles, explain the limit and obtain a
supported explicit roster before dispatch. Never simulate independent agents.

Use the `model_selection` shape in the binding guide. Required fields are `profile`
(economy/balanced/thorough/custom), `confirmed`, `checked_at`, `availability_source`,
`catalog` and `roles` (grounding/workers/outflanker/chair). `worker_overrides` may map
an exact analysis lens to its own assignment. Include `effort` and catalog `efforts`
only when the selected model and tool actually support that control, and record the checked
tool capability as `binding.supports_effort: true`. Without it, omit role `effort` and use
provider defaults. See the binding guide's concrete field example. Custom-agent binding uses
provider-default effort.

Recheck for each new run and after an availability/host/account change. Stored
preferences and aliases do not establish current availability or backend versions.
Keep per-run choices private; persist a preference only when requested. If binding
fails, preserve completed roles and get the user's replacement choice. `retry` can
change only the failed role, within its existing retry allowance.

Report requested model separately from runtime-observed identity. Set observed
identity only from exposed host metadata; an LLM identifying itself is not proof.
Explain missing identity evidence or conflicting names rather than hiding fallback.

# Sources and Decision Council skill learning

Read when Decision Council reviews workspace code, an IssueTracker ticket or a CodeReview PR, or uses the user's KB.
The main conversation identifies the relevant sources; grounding turns inspected evidence into the
shared factbase. Workers remain independent and do not fetch their own competing versions.

## Select and read the sources

Use the user's current workspace when the question concerns it. If several workspace roots
or IssueTracker sites match, clarify only the ambiguous target. The repository distributing Decision Council is not
automatically the subject. Resolve paths, issue keys and PR links from actual context rather than
requiring the user to list every file. Inspect only sources relevant to the agreed decision.

| Source | What to inspect | What to preserve in the evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Workspace | Local instructions and design documents, relevant implementation, tests/configuration and changes | Workspace root, file/line, actual branch/commit and any uncommitted differences relevant to the claim. Reading a test is not running it. |
| IssueTracker ticket | Summary, description, acceptance criteria where present, status, relevant comments and linked issues | Site plus issue key/URL, field or comment reference and retrieval time. Ticket statements describe intent or reported behavior, not proof that code implements it. |
| CodeReview PR | Description, actual diff and surrounding code, source/target revisions, relevant comments, approvals and build/check results | Host, repository, PR number/URL, inspected revisions and locations. Approvals or green checks do not by themselves prove the requirement is met. |

For a combined request, compare the ticket's intended outcome with the PR diff and relevant workspace
implementation. Do not assume that an open checkout is the PR's current revision. Make any mismatch
explicit before using local files as evidence for that PR. Check relevant pagination and truncation;
unread comments, omitted files or missing build results remain gaps. The review does not post comments,
change a ticket, approve/merge a PR, or edit the subject.

Use read tools already available and authorized in the current execution environment, such as workspace
tools, a configured MCP integration or an approved authenticated CLI. Inspect their actual capabilities;
do not invent connector names or assume that IssueTracker access also grants CodeReview access. A URL alone does
not establish access. Do not search other skills for credentials or copy tokens into prompts/reports.

If the required integration is unavailable, say which source cannot be read. Use a supplied export or
pasted excerpt when appropriate and attribute it as supplied material, with its date and limitations.
If missing evidence prevents the decision, say so; do not replace inaccessible private code with public
documentation or treat a failed fetch as an empty result.

When only the main conversation can access a connector, fetch the authorized source there before
initializing the run. Save the relevant excerpts with their original URLs, revisions, retrieval dates
and gaps in a private source packet; include its path in `primary_sources` so grounding can read it.
Keep `source_targets` pointed at the actual workspace/ticket/PR. The packet is a transport for attributed
evidence, not a claim that grounding itself fetched those sources. If neither context can access the
source, record it as unavailable.

## Record coverage, including failures

Add identified targets to the request. The user does not write this data:

```json
"source_targets": [
  {"kind": "workspace", "ref": "/actual/workspace/root"},
  {"kind": "jira", "ref": "https://actual-site/browse/ACTUAL-KEY"},
  {"kind": "bitbucket_pr", "ref": "https://actual-host/path/to/pr"}
]
```

These are placeholders, not sources to fetch. The optional machine-readable kinds `jira` and `bitbucket_pr` are retained legacy identifiers for compatibility; no data-format migration or connector is introduced. Generic IssueTracker/CodeReview labels do not imply support for arbitrary service APIs. Supported kinds are `workspace`, `jira`, `bitbucket_pr`,
`document` and `web`. Omit irrelevant kinds. For a question based only on the user's description, an
empty target list is valid. Every listed target must appear exactly once in grounding's response:

```json
"source_coverage": [
  {
    "kind": "jira",
    "ref": "exact reference from source_targets",
    "status": "partial",
    "as_of": "actual retrieval date/time",
    "detail": "Description and acceptance criteria read. Comments unavailable; later discussion may change scope."
  }
]
```

Status is `read`, `partial` or `unavailable`. `read` means the material needed for this scoped review
was inspected, not that an entire system was audited. Put revisions, actual tool failures and the
effect of omissions in `detail`. Fact references still identify the original file/line, ticket field,
comment or PR diff location. The coordinator checks coverage structure and carries it through the
human checkpoint, all downstream prompts and report; it cannot prove the claimed access occurred.
Completion describes the agent workflow. Partial evidence must still limit the verdict.

## Reuse improvements to Decision Council's method

The KB exists only to improve the skill's working method. It is not a project knowledge base or
result archive. Case facts, findings, verdicts, IssueTracker/PR details and domain knowledge belong in run
reports and supporting files, even when the user confirms them.

Read the private root from the configured location and inspect its `council_kb.md` before framing.
Select relevant process improvements: clearer scope questions, better source checks, agent handoffs,
model-selection procedure or clearer explanations. Keep their context and limits. Ignore legacy case
content if present; preserve the user's file. A missing KB on first use is normal.

The main conversation applies relevant guidance to framing and model selection, then includes a
small selection for the agents in `skill_lessons`:

```json
"skill_lessons": [
  {
    "purpose": "skill_improvement",
    "lesson": "Decision Council should label PR descriptions separately from inspected code in the fact review.",
    "context": "Reviews combining intent and implementation",
    "limits": "Evidence presentation only; does not determine the verdict.",
    "source": "personal KB path and entry ID"
  }
]
```

Each agent receives these as method guidance, separately from the case evidence. Apply only guidance
relevant to that role. It cannot override the workflow, agreed scope or chosen models. Never cite the
KB as proof about a case or promote it into the factbase. Current source material establishes facts.
For model lessons, retain a selection principle rather than treating an old model name as available.

## Save a confirmed lesson

After delivering a completed or failed review, offer one optional reflection on **how Decision Council worked**.
Save only a method improvement the user supplies or explicitly confirms. For example:

- Save: "Decision Council should check whether the local checkout matches the PR revision before reviewing."
- Keep in the report: "PR 17 does not meet the ticket's freshness requirement."

Write the entry JSON in the private run folder and invoke the coordinator:

```text
python3 <skill>/scripts/council_run.py learn --run <run> --entry <lesson.json>
```

```json
{
  "purpose": "skill_improvement",
  "confirmed": true,
  "lesson": "The confirmed improvement to Decision Council's working method",
  "context": "Which part of the process this applies to",
  "limits": "Where this process guidance does not apply",
  "confirmation": "The actual user reply supplying or confirming this method improvement"
}
```

The helper requires the skill-improvement purpose and rejects additional fields such as results or
verdicts. It cannot judge the meaning of arbitrary prose or authenticate a recorded reply: the main
conversation must check that the entry improves the method and record the real reply. Do not save
case knowledge under a method label.

The KB receives the improvement, context, limits, date, entry ID and originating run ID. The actual
reply is retained in `runs/<id>/learning/<entry-id>.json`; it is not copied into the KB because it may
mention results. Existing KB content is preserved, concurrent writes are serialized and identical
lesson/context/limits entries are skipped. The packaged KB and run report are not modified. Return
the saved KB path, or say the entry was already present. Later runs reuse the process improvement
without importing this case's outcome.

## Integration references

These describe available mechanisms, not proof that a user's account has them configured:

- [Optional legacy Jira API: issues and fields](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/jira/platform/rest/v3/api-group-issues/)
- [Optional legacy Bitbucket API: pull requests, diffs, comments and checks](https://developer.atlassian.com/cloud/bitbucket/rest/api-group-pullrequests/)

Use the actual host's integration for Data Center or other deployments; do not send credentials to a
Cloud endpoint just because a reference above describes it.
